what_changed.headline: Long-end real-rate and supply pressure remains the dominant rates risk
what_changed.significance: ING attributes higher long yields to issuance pressure and AI-linked productivity expectations rather than inflation expectations; it expects further curve steepening.
what_changed.transmission: Persistent supply and real-rate pressure raises discount rates and refinancing costs, particularly for long-duration assets.

what_changed.headline: Euro-area inflation rose mainly through energy, while activity remains resilient
what_changed.significance: German headline inflation reached 2.9% year-on-year in August, while core and services inflation eased or held steady; euro-area surveys improved.
what_changed.transmission: Energy risks support near-term rate pressure, but limited pass-through and resilient activity complicate the ECB reaction function.

what_changed.headline: Hyperscaler borrowing is becoming material in euro credit
what_changed.significance: US big tech represents just under 10% of new euro non-financial corporate issuance, with roughly €40 billion outstanding; ECB analysis warns of potential future crowding-out.
what_changed.transmission: Large, long-maturity issuance can absorb portfolio capacity, widen risk premia and build long-end corporate supply.

executive_decisions.development: Treat duration as vulnerable to supply and real-rate repricing rather than assuming inflation expectations are the primary driver.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: The cited analysis identifies issuance and real-rate forces as the key long-end pressure.
executive_decisions.transmission: Higher real yields weigh on long-duration rates, credit and growth equities.

executive_decisions.development: Monitor the September US labour report as the key near-term test of the hawkish Fed repricing.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: Available sources disagree on whether weak employment or sticky inflation should dominate policy.
executive_decisions.transmission: A weak report would challenge higher front-end rates; persistent inflation or resilient activity would reinforce them.

macro_themes.theme: Supply, fiscal and AI investment are lifting the long-end risk premium
macro_themes.thesis: Large public and private investment needs are competing for capital, while AI financing adds corporate bond supply.
macro_themes.market_implication: Long-duration rates and credit remain exposed to higher real yields, issuance and refinancing premia.

observed_facts.text: Hyperscalers are projected to require more than USD 1 trillion of capital expenditure by 2028.
US long yields have risen alongside higher real-rate pressure and issuance concerns.

inferences.text: Sustained AI and fiscal investment could keep duration risk elevated even if inflation expectations remain contained.

conflicting_evidence.text: Euro-area corporate issuance has so far produced limited spillovers to other issuers.

unresolved_questions: Whether investor capacity expands sufficiently to absorb future hyperscaler issuance.
Whether AI capital expenditure converts into durable productivity and earnings growth.

transmission.implication: Bearish for long duration if real yields and supply pressure persist.
Higher-quality long-maturity supply may widen relative premia and crowd other issuers.
Higher discount rates challenge long-duration growth valuations, especially when expectations are elevated.

catalysts: Evidence on AI monetisation and returns
invalidation_conditions: Weak activity materially lowers issuance and real yields.
AI investment slows without broader financing pressure.

asset_views.thesis: Front-end yields remain vulnerable to renewed tightening expectations, subject to the labour-market data.
asset_views.transmission: A credible inflation response would lift expected policy rates; weak employment would reverse that pressure.

US core PCE and services inflation remain above target.
The labour market shows weak payroll growth and soft wages.
risks: Weak August payrolls or rising unemployment.
Supply-driven inflation fades without second-round effects.
asset_views.invalidation_condition: Clear labour-market deterioration alongside falling underlying inflation.

evidence.text: Fed hike expectations rose after Warsh's speech, according to market commentary.

counterevidence.text: J.P. Morgan argues the labour market is weaker and less inflationary than the Fed chair portrayed.

asset_views.thesis: Growing hyperscaler issuance raises medium-term supply and concentration risk for euro investment-grade credit.
asset_views.transmission: Large long-maturity deals can absorb investor balance sheets and raise required compensation for other issuers.
drivers: Hyperscalers represent just under 10% of new euro non-financial corporate issuance.
Hyperscaler spreads have increased as issuance expectations rose.
risks: Investor demand expands with the supply.
Strong balance sheets and high ratings limit default concerns.
asset_views.catalyst: Further large hyperscaler bond issuance or weaker deal cover.
asset_views.invalidation_condition: Issuance slows and spreads stabilise without spillovers to other sectors.

evidence.text: Hyperscaler bonds outstanding total around €40 billion and their share of reverse-Yankee issuance nearly doubled between 2025 and 2026.

counterevidence.text: Cover ratios for euro-area issuers remained strong and little changed during 2026.

signposts: Labour data do not materially deteriorate.
